why: Single source for the required/optional GitHub Release asset contract (see AmbiqAI/ns-cmsis-nn#376, #274, #339). The same list used to be hand-maintained in .github/workflows/release.yml, scripts/ci/audit_release_assets.sh and docs/guides/releases.md, with nothing relating the three: an asset added only to release.yml would pass at release time and never be audited nightly. Adding an asset now means editing this file and the docs table; scripts/check_release_asset_manifest.py fails the merge if the two disagree, and both consumers expand this file through scripts/ci/release_assets.py rather than building names themselves.
contract_floor_why: First release cut under this contract. v7.25.0 and older shipped a different, smaller asset shape (loose per-cpu .a files, gcc only) and are not judged by a contract that postdates them.
promotion_why: Repository variable, deliberately an operator switch rather than an inference from whether an Arm license secret is configured: that secret was configured throughout the period armclang published nothing at all, so keying off it would promote assets the pipeline has never once produced, and a required-but-unproducible asset makes every release unrecoverably red (#279).
audit_promotable_why: scripts/ci/audit_release_assets.sh never promotes the optional assets, even when ARMCLANG_REQUIRED is set: that variable is a point-in-time operator switch, and applying it retroactively would flag historical releases that shipped complete under the contract of their day.
non_asset_rows_why: Rows the docs table carries that are not GitHub Release assets. They are listed here so the docs table can be checked as a whole set: an asset-shaped row nobody registered is the drift this manifest exists to end, and a checker that silently ignored unknown rows would wave it through.
